unit_definition: One record per (law, date). seq 0 is the law's publication, every later known in-force date is a revision. Language versions of one act are one law, so a trilingual consolidation is one event.

measures.lines: lines added + removed by the revision, from git numstat on the consolidation commits. Needs two versions of a file to diff, so it is federal law in practice — the cantonal corpus holds one version per law.
measures.words: words added + removed by the revision, and the magnitude that covers both scopes. Federal revisions are diffed from the two markdown versions in this corpus; cantonal revisions from the version series LexFind publishes for every cantonal act, whose PDFs are fetched and diffed the same way. Words rather than lines because a line means different things in the two sources — one markdown paragraph is several lines of a PDF — while a word means the same in both.
measures.articles_publication/articles_revision: articles of the law the event applies to, from the markdown body. Covers federal and cantonal law alike, because every law in the corpus has a text. It is the law's CURRENT size credited to each of its events, so recent years are exact and older ones are anachronistic.
